newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day Cetes rates rise on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day Cetes rates rise on speculation.

text.p: Mexico's same-day Cetes rates rose 100 basis points to 30.20 percent at the close of trade on Tuesday, pushed up by speculation, dealers said.
However, the decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee to keep U.S. rates unchanged could help Mexican interest rates to fall on Wednesday, they said.

"We are expecting that with the confirmation that there will not be a change in rates in the U.S. and if the primary (Cetes) auction follows as expected, then from tomorrow the rates could start to fall a little," said one dealer.
A survey by Reuters found expectations of an increase of 94 basis points in the 28-day paper at the primary auction.
Trade was moderate in the morning as dealers waited for the Fed's decision.
Bank notes and acceptances closed down 35 basis points to 30.60 percent.
Dealers expect a rise in primary rates at Banco de Mexico's Cetes auction on Tuesday due in part to expected increases in inflation.
Banco de Mexico injected liquidity worth 7.348 billion pesos via four credit auctions. For Wednesday, maturing credits are seen at 5.099 billion pesos.
